subject: Dedicated pool — concurrency skew, burst policy and recommended GPU footprint
messages:
From: Sasha Dimitrov <sasha@acuitylabs.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acuitylabs.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: what do we actually need?

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We want to lock down committed capacity guidance for our main inference path (customer-facing chat + long-form summarization) and need your recommendation on GPU pool sizing, burst policy, and what a realistic reserved-commit looks like from a cost/discount perspective. High-level footprint:~
- Typical daily volume: ~28k requests/day (weekdays) with heavy concentration 10:00–14:00 PT.
- Peak simultaneous interactive sessions observed: ~220 concurrent generators during peak 11:30–12:30 PT (spike events up to ~560 for short windows).
- Model mix: ~70% Llama-13B (quantized q4_0-like profile), 30% MPT-30B (more expensive tail).
- Average prompt in tokens: 900; average model-generated tokens: 1,200 (so ~2.1k total per request).
- Target latency SLO: p50 ~300ms, p95 < 1.2s for interactive users.

We can share a small workload sample (CSV) if that helps. Two asks:
1) Rough pool size you’d recommend for a 12-month reserved commit that meets the SLOs above (with a modest burst buffer).
2) How Redwood typically structures burst credits vs guaranteed capacity and where discounts kick in for committed GPU-hours.

We’re trying to align procurement timing, so any preliminary numbers + a sketch of pricing tiers would be really helpful.

Thanks —
Sasha
Head of Product, Acuity Labs

(Attachment: acuity_workload_sample.csv)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Dimitrov <sasha@acuitylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: what do we actually need?

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sending the sample — that will help a lot. Quick clarifying questions before I drop concrete numbers:
- Are those peak spikes (to ~560) correlated with any particular job type (batch import vs interactive chat)?
- What fraction of requests are cacheable / repeat prompts (we often get big wins from prefix/KV cache for Q&A and summarization).
- Do you expect the model mix to shift toward larger models in the next 6–12 months? If yes, by how much?

Prelim, based on the numbers you provided and our throughput profiles for your model mix, here’s a back‑of‑the‑envelope:
- Workload compute need at peak: ~220 steady concurrent generators. Assuming average generation is 1,200 tokens and effective token output rate per A100-class GPU for your mixed workload ~500 tokens/sec (weighted between the two models after quantization and batching). That yields ~2.4k tokens/sec required at steady peak per cluster (220 * (1,200 tokens / avg gen time)). Conservatively estimating gen time ~2.4s/request across profiles, we size to sustained tokens/sec need ~13k tokens/sec.
- With 500 tokens/sec per GPU, that maps to ~26 GPUs to meet steady peak.
- To cover brief spikes to ~560 we recommend a burst pool (autoscale + pre-warmed spot-style capacity) of +10–14 GPUs for short windows, or a higher guaranteed buffer if you want to avoid any capacity-based throttling.
- Suggested reserved commit: baseline 28–30 GPUs (A100-class equivalence) reserved with an additional 12 GPUs available as burst credits that can be used across the month.

Tradeoffs and options:
- If you’re comfortable with slight P95 variability, a 24–28 GPU commit + 12 burst is lower cost. If the interactive experience must be consistent (no throttling during spikes), push to 34–36 GPU guaranteed.
- We can also mix instance types: cheaper 80GB A100s for the quantized 13B path and a small pool of 4–6 faster RTX-class nodes for the MPT-30B tail to reduce cost while keeping p95 in check.

I’ll loop Ben for pricing assumptions and a draft packaging matrix. If you can confirm the clarifying answers, I’ll convert this into a proposal PDF.

Best,
Priya
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Dimitrov <sasha@acuitylabs.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: what do we actually need?

Sasha —

Adding pricing context and discount mechanics. Numbers below are illustrative; we’ll formalize in the SOW once we agree on footprint.

Option A — Cost-sensitive (min guaranteed + burst credits):
- Commit: 28 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (monthly).
- Burst pool: 12 GPU-hours reserved as burst credits that can be consumed when autoscaler requires extra capacity (we commonly structure burst as a monthly/hourly credit pool).
- 12-month term discount: 18% off list on committed GPU-hours; 24-month term: 26% off.
- Onboarding credit: one month of 4 GPUs free for performance tuning and KV-cache warmup.

Option B — SLA-sensitive (consistent p95):
- Commit: 34 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved.
- Burst pool: 6 GPUs for extreme events only.
- 12-month term discount: 22% off; 24-month: 30% off.
- We include a 99.9% availability SLA for the dedicated pool and a dedicated onboarding window.

Notes on packaging mechanics:
- Burst credits incur a lower marginal price than on-demand; unused burst credits roll over up to 20% month-to-month.
- If you choose a hybrid pool (cheaper GPUs + small RTX pool for heavy models), we price each tier independently and apply an aggregated discount on committed spend.

I’ll add a quick table to the PDF with monthly committed GPU-hours, effective hourly rate after discount, and expected monthly cost for both options once Priya confirms the final GPU count.

Ben
Sr. Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Dimitrov <sasha@acuitylabs.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acuitylabs.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: what do we actually need?

Thanks Priya / Ben — this is really helpful. A few quick notes:
- The 560 spikes are almost entirely interactive (campaign-driven surges) and last ~4–9 minutes. They’re not batch.
- Cacheability: roughly 22% of requests hit prior prefixes (interactive follow-ups), so we’d expect caching to knock down effective compute a bit.
- Model mix: plan to keep it roughly stable for the next 6 months; we’ll reevaluate as new fine-tuned variants roll out.

We attached a sample export from our logs (acuity_workload_sample.csv) with timestamps, model id, token counts, and observed latency. Can you incorporate the cacheability into the sizing math and re-run the numbers? Also — we’ll need the SOW and a shortlist of contract terms (data retention, audit logs, KMS) for procurement.

Appreciate the prompt turnaround; happy to jump on a call if that’s easier.

—Sasha

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Dimitrov <sasha@acuitylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: what do we actually need?

Sasha —

Appreciate the sample — we ran it against our throughput models and revised the recommendation to reflect your ~22% cache hit rate. Summary (concise):
- Adjusted steady peak compute need: reduced by ~18% once prefix/KV caching and request deduplication are applied (some conservatism retained for regeneration variance).
- Revised recommended reserved commit: 23–25 A100-equivalent GPUs guaranteed.
- Recommended burst pool: 12 GPUs available for short spikes (pre-warmed autoscale, 0–10 minute spin-down).
- Hybrid optimization: shift ~6 of the guaranteed GPUs to cheaper 80GB A100 capacity for the quantized 13B path, keep 4 higher-memory/FP32-capable nodes for the MPT tail. This preserves p95 while lowering cost ~12% vs an all-A100 pool.
- Packaging suggestion (commercial): start with a 12-month commit at 24 GPUs + 12 burst credits. Pricing Tier: ~18% discount on committed GPU-hours, onboarding credit (one month of 4 GPUs), and a 30-day performance window to validate KV cache savings.

Next steps: I’ll upload a proposal PDF (redwood_pool_proposal_v1.pdf) and a draft SOW with data retention & KMS language. If this aligns, Ben will convert to a HubSpot deal and issue an initial term sheet.

Proposed call to finalize: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:00 PT — does that work for your team?

Cheers,
Priya
